item.text:
# Bola Ahmed Tinubu, 2024: 3B.5 research note

Bottom line: I found some lawful, institution-building moves, but the strongest 2024 evidence is that security tools were used coercively against protest, journalists, and detainees. I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence of a formal nationwide emergency declaration; the control pattern was mostly ordinary policing, treason/cybercrime law, and administrative crackdown.

**Positive / narrower-use evidence**
- [We Will Transform Nigeria Police Into Modern, Professional Force - President Tinubu](https://statehouse.gov.ng/we-will-transform-nigeria-police-into-modern-professional-force-president-tinubu/) — State House, April 16, 2024. Tinubu said his administration was making the police more modern, professional, accountable, and better trained. This is supportive but aspirational; it does not itself prove complaint handling or independent oversight. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.4`, `3B.2`.
- [My Resolve To Enhance Nigeria’s Security Unwavering - President Tinubu](https://statehouse.gov.ng/my-resolve-to-enhance-nigerias-security-unwavering-president-tinubu/) — State House, April 22, 2024. Tinubu backed state policing as a way to improve accountability and safeguard civil liberties. This is the clearest policy-level signal for narrower, lawful security governance. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.4`, `3B.2`.
- [President Tinubu Appoints New Leadership for Police Service Commission and Nigerian Police Trust Fund](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-appoints-new-leadership-for-police-service-commission-and-nigerian-police-trust-fund/) — State House, June 10, 2024. New PSC and Trust Fund leadership supports civilian oversight capacity over policing, though the release does not describe a complaint system or abuse-investigation mechanism. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.4`, `3B.2`.
- [Tinubu orders probe of security agents involved in arrest, detention of minors](https://www.thecable.ng/tinubu-orders-probe-of-security-agents-involved-in-arrest-detention-of-minors/) — TheCable, November 4, 2024. Tinubu ordered a probe into the arrest, detention, and treatment of minors detained over protests and said involved officers would be investigated and disciplined if needed. This is the strongest direct positive evidence for narrow, lawful corrective use of administrative power. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.4`, `3B.2`.
- [UNICEF Welcomes President Tinubu’s Order for Immediate Release of Detained Children](https://www.unicef.org/nigeria/press-releases/unicef-welcomes-president-tinubus-order-immediate-release-detained-children) — UNICEF Nigeria, November 5, 2024. UNICEF confirmed Tinubu ordered the release of detained children and young people. This shows reactive remediation after abuse became public, not a mature system of oversight. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.4`, `3B.2`.
- [Detained Endbad Governance Suspects Released - Vice President Shettima Hands Over Pardoned Suspects To State Governments](https://fmino.gov.ng/detained-endbad-governance-suspects-released-vice-president-shettima-hands-over-pardoned-suspects-to-state-governments/) — Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation, November 5, 2024. The ministry said the detainees were released in line with Tinubu’s directive and handed to state governments for rehabilitation and reintegration. This supports partial corrective action after the crackdown. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.4`, `3B.2`.

**Negative / coercive-use evidence**
- [Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024) — Freedom House, 2024. Freedom House said the Cybercrimes Act was amended in February 2024, but its cyberstalking provision had long been used to arrest or imprison journalists and activists. This is strong negative evidence that a security law still functioned as a repression tool. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.2`, `3B.3`.
- [Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting](https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/) — Committee to Protect Journalists, October 3, 2024. CPJ said four journalists were charged under the Cybercrimes Act despite the February reform, showing continued use of security-law charges against press activity. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.2`, `3B.3`.
- [Nigeria charges protesters with treason, inciting military](https://theprint.in/world/nigeria-charges-protesters-with-treason-inciting-military/2249248/) — Reuters via ThePrint, September 2, 2024. Prosecutors charged protesters with treason and alleged they wanted to destabilize Nigeria and incite mutiny. That is strong evidence of security-law escalation and intimidation rather than narrowly lawful enforcement. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`.
- [Nigeria charges 76, including minors, with treason after August protests](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nigeria-charges-76-including-minors-with-treason-after-august-protests-3698000) — Reuters via Investing.com, November 1, 2024. The government expanded the case to 76 defendants, including 30 minors, after the protests. This strengthens the reading of collective punishment and punitive control. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`.
- [Nigerian police teargas protesters, arrest dozens](https://theprint.in/world/nigerian-police-teargas-protesters-arrest-dozens/2206531/) — Reuters via ThePrint, August 3, 2024. Police arrested dozens and used tear gas to disperse protesters trying to march on government offices, while also keeping demonstrations at the outskirts of major cities. That looks more like containment/intimidation than narrow, rights-protective crowd management. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`.
- [Nigeria’s police chief warns against Kenyan-style protests](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Nigeria-s-police-chief-warns-against-Kenyan-style-protests-47446946/) — Reuters via MarketScreener, July 23, 2024. The police chief framed the coming protests in a security-threat register before they began, which helped normalize a crackdown posture. This is indirect, but it points toward intimidation rather than neutral administration. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.3`, `3B.2`.
- [Nigeria security forces deploy, government offers dialogue as protests loom](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462) — Reuters via Investing.com, July 31, 2024. The government said it was open to dialogue, but security forces were simultaneously deployed in major cities. Mixed on its face, but the coercive preparedness undercuts the claim of narrowly lawful restraint. Question IDs: `3B.5`; other: `3B.2`.

**Search gap**
- I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence that Tinubu declared a nationwide state of emergency, imposed a broad emergency regime, or publicly launched a sweeping surveillance program.
- I also did **not** find strong evidence of a transparent, independent review process for security-force abuse before the November minors probe and release order.
- The main pattern in 2024 was ordinary-law coercion: protest policing, treason charges, and cybercrime enforcement used in ways rights groups said chilled dissent.
